sector_model: Grocery retail: comparable sales, new store productivity, FCF after gross capex, lease liabilities treated as debt-like.
thesis: Sprouts Farmers Market (Nasdaq: SFM), healthy grocery. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-28) and 8-K EX-99.1 read. Net sales Q3 2,304.7M +5% (new stores +128.8M), comparable sales -0.9% (transactions -3.3%, basket +2.5%, cyclospora outbreak -0.6 pt) vs +5.9% a year ago; gross margin 38.2% vs 38.7% (shrink +0.4%); Q3 net income 113.4M vs 120.1M, 9M 406.3M vs 433.8M (-6%). 504 stores (15 opened in the quarter). TTM revenue 9,108.4M, NI 496.2M, OCF 693.7M, capex 356.4M gross, FCF 337.3M (7.5% yield, 6.9% after SBC 28.5M). Close 48.81 (2026-11-20, two sources agree) x 92.23M shares = 4,502M: 9.1x TTM earnings, 10.2x FY2026 guided EPS ~4.80, 2.9x book. No revolver borrowings (600M), cash 228.7M, finance and other debt 133.1M, operating lease liabilities 2,102.5M. Buybacks 299.2M in 9M, share count 95.9M to 92.7M since December. Guidance: Q4 comparable sales -2% to -4%, Q4 EPS 0.47-0.51 (includes 53rd week worth about 0.16), FY EBIT ~605M, capex ~310M net, 42 net new stores; management will invest more in price. Possible mispricing view: market extrapolates negative comps and margin investment; the countervailing facts are unit growth of about 9% and a fully self-funded balance sheet. Not established.
counterthesis: Q4 EPS guide of 0.47-0.51 compares with roughly 0.9 a year earlier (Q4 2025 NI about 89.8M from FY less 9M, derived, share count approximate), so earnings are guided down about 45% including a 53rd week, and management says price investments will pressure margins into fiscal 2027; comparable transactions fell 3.3%; incentive compensation fell 15.2M in Q3 which flatters SG&A; operating lease liabilities of 2.1B are debt-like and growing with 42 new stores (capex up 62% in 9M); a 9x multiple may be a fair price for a business whose comps turned negative; securities and derivative litigation is pending; I have not compared peers.
invalidation: Drop if comparable sales stay negative into 2027 with gross margin below 38%, new store productivity weakens, or lease-adjusted leverage rises. Study further only with peers, the call transcript and 10-K audit matters read and quote origins documented.
